## Objective
- Complete the existing SKYBOUND jet-flying game so it is fully playable.

## Requirements
- Finish the game without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.
- Save check screenshots as small JPEGs at viewport widths up to 1280px, and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use the existing Three.js procedural-world game, vendored locally through the import map.
- Connect the flight, world, and UI code in `src/main.js`.

### Completed
- Added game initialization, flight controls, cameras, HUD/minimap, waypoint progression, pause/restart/help/sound behavior, and animation loop in `src/main.js`.
- Fixed `Jet.reset()` to reset `distanceFlown` in `src/jet.js`.
- Fixed audio update logic so muted sound remains muted during flight.

1. Continue browser validation, including crash/restart behavior; address any defects found.

- `src/main.js`: Game initialization, UI wiring, controls, and update loop.
- `src/jet.js`: Flight simulation, jet model, reset, and crash behavior.
- `src/world.js`: World generation, waypoint gates, and minimap source.
- `index.html`: Game UI and module entry point.
- `style.css`: Game and HUD styling.

- Changes are uncommitted; `src/main.js` is untracked.

SKYBOUND is playable end to end. I connected the flight simulation, procedural world, HUD, waypoint route, controls, pause/help/camera/sound options, and restart flow in `src/main.js`. I also fixed `Jet.reset()` in `src/jet.js` so the flown-distance counter resets with the aircraft.

**Validation:** tested flight controls and boost, pause/resume, camera and help toggles, crash behavior and crash restart. JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed; the browser console showed no errors.

**Screenshot:** captured and inspected [`screenshots/skybound-final.jpg`](screenshots/skybound-final.jpg) at 1280 × 800. The screenshot directory is ignored by Git.

**Assumption:** this is a relaxed, single-player scenic flight game, so I kept the existing no-enemies direction and treated the gold gates as optional waypoints.
